subject: Follow-up: Pricing & batching assumptions for Acme - continuous batching & concurrency
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Pricing & batching assumptions for Acme - continuous batching & concurrency

Hi Sarah — great to meet today, thanks for the thoughtful conversation. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can size pricing and batching assumptions for the PoC / initial roll-out: 

Call recap
- Workload: interactive agent/chat for internal ops + a smaller async batch scoring job for recommendations. Primary traffic expected to be chat.
- Prompt/response sizes you quoted: ~60 tokens average prompt, ~80 tokens average response (so ~140 tokens total per request).
- Expected token volumes: short-term PoC ~50M tokens/month; 6-12 month production target ~800M-1.2B tokens/month (you said ~1B in target scenario).
- Traffic pattern: fairly steady during business hours with predictable peaks (roughly 2-3x baseline), not huge once warmed; you mentioned many concurrent short sessions rather than large single long generations.

Key asks / assumptions we need you to confirm
1) Confirmation of average prompt/response tokens (we used 140 tokens/interaction in our back-of-envelope).
2) Typical concurrency: what do you expect for steady-state concurrent sessions (avg vs peak)? e.g., avg concurrency 10-50, peak 200+?
3) Any strict cost target (e.g., target $/1M tokens or monthly budget range) we should aim for in our pricing proposal?

Pricing & batching note (high-level)
- With continuous batching and prefix caching, we commonly see ~20-35% unit cost reduction vs naive per-request serving for chat-like workloads, depending on sequence lengths and cache hit rates.
- For sizing, if we assume 1B tokens/month and continuous batching that achieves ~25% savings, that materially moves the economics vs no-batching.

Next steps
- Can you reply with the concurrency numbers and confirm the average tokens?
- I attached a mutual action plan (Acme_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx) and the requested security questionnaire stub. If that looks good, we can schedule a technical deep-dive with Aditya (engineer) to align on batching behavior and a short procurement checklist for finance.

Thanks — I’ll draft a short pricing sketch once we have your concurrency + token confirmation.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Acme_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet) | Acme_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.io>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acme.io>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pricing & batching assumptions for Acme - continuous batching & concurrency

Hi Camila — thanks for the note and the MMP. Confirming the numbers we discussed and adding a couple of clarifications: 

Confirmed numbers
- Average prompt: 65 tokens, average response: 75 tokens => ~140 tokens total (happy to use 140 as your estimate).
- PoC: 40-60M tokens/month (some fluctuation).
- Target production: ~1B tokens/month within 9-12 months if PoC looks good.

Concurrency / traffic profile
- Baseline steady-state concurrency: roughly 30-60 concurrent sessions during business hours.
- Peak concurrency: up to ~220 concurrent sessions for short bursts (no more than ~15-20 minutes).
- Most sessions are short (1-3 exchanges) which means latency sensitivity is moderate - sub-second token latency matters, but we prioritize cost/throughput over extreme p99 latency.

Budget & target unit economics
- Finance has given a target budget band for model inference of ~$15k- $35k/month for early PoC (we can stretch for production if justified).
- We’re trying to understand unit economics and your expected $/1M tokens guidance. For the PoC stage we’d like to see pricing that keeps PoC monthly cost under ~$20k if possible.

Happy to schedule the technical deep-dive with Aditya - can do Thu 9th or Fri 10th. Michael (cc'd) will coordinate procurement/PO questions after the technical call.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Liu
Head of Platform, Acme Cloud
sarah.liu@acme.io

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pricing & batching assumptions for Acme - continuous batching & concurrency

Camila — quick pricing note for the thread so you can set expectations with Sarah. Numbers below are initial sketches and will change after the technical deep dive, but we should be within range: 

Assumptions (for sketch)
- Token size: 140 tokens/interaction
- PoC volume: 50M tokens/mo (use midpoint)
- Prod volume: 1B tokens/mo
- Continuous batching benefit: 20-30% cost reduction vs naive per-request baseline for chat workloads with short sequences; higher (up to ~35%) if caching hit-rate is good and requests are steady-flow.

Pricing sketches (unit economics)
- Baseline unit (no batching) reference: assume $40/1M tokens (placeholder; actual depends on model size/quantization).
- With continuous batching (25% reduction) => ~$30/1M tokens.
- With strong caching + quantization tradeoffs we could be in the $20-25/1M tokens band at scale.

Impact on monthly cost (approx)
- PoC (50M tokens): $1.5k- $2.0k at $30/1M tokens (note: depends on model choice).
- Production (1B tokens): $20k- $30k at $20- $30/1M tokens - aligns with Acme’s stretch budget 

Notes for technical deep-dive
- Need to validate request distribution (interarrival times), sequence length distribution, and any heavy tails (long sessions) that hurt batching effectiveness.
- Also confirm whether you can provide short traces/sample logs for a day of traffic - that will let us simulate batching and estimate realistic unit economics.

I’ll be on the technical call with Aditya if helpful.

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.io>, Michael Torres <michael.torres@acme.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pricing & batching assumptions for Acme - continuous batching & concurrency

Hi Sarah / Michael — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on your concurrency guidance and Marissa’s sketches above, here’s a concrete next-step plan and a tighter pricing expectation for PoC: 

Confirmed numbers
- Average tokens/interaction: 140 (confirmed)
- PoC target: 50M tokens/mo (we’ll price to keep this under ~$20k if possible)
- Steady concurrency: 30-60; peak bursts up to 220 (short)

Tight PoC pricing expectation (sketch)
- Working target: $25/1M tokens (assumes continuous batching ~25% savings and mid-range model quantization).
- At 50M tokens/mo => estimated monthly cost ~ $1,250 (note: this is incremental inference spend; we’ll include any per-tenant fixed fees in the MMP).
- If production ramps to 1B tokens/mo and batching/caching behave as expected, run-rate could be ~$25k/mo at $25/1M tokens (discounts/commits apply).

Technical ask ahead of deep-dive
- Send 24-48 hours of anonymized request logs (timestamps, request/response token counts) so we can model batching. A sample CSV is ideal; we can share a template.
- Confirm which model variant you expect to use (we’ll map model size to unit reference).

Scheduling
- Aditya is available Fri 10th 10:30-11:30 PT for a short technical deep-dive; happy to book if that works.

Next steps (mutual action plan)
- I’ve attached the MMP and security questionnaire we referenced. If you confirm the PoC token target and sign the MMP (or ack via email), we’ll queue a technical model/benchmark and give you a more formal price quote and playbook for batching/concurrency tuning.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
